falsifiable_hypothesis: During a completed positive BTC/ETH 24-hour market context, an extreme negative 4-hour BTC return residual relative to ETH represents temporary BTC underreaction and predicts a positive BTC catch-up over the following 24 hours large enough to survive retail spot costs.
economic_mechanism: Shared crypto information is incorporated unevenly across BTC and ETH. Conditional on positive ETH participation and positive joint 24-hour context, an idiosyncratic BTC underreaction may mean-revert as liquidity and attention rotate back to BTC. The null is that the residual is contemporaneous noise or adverse BTC-specific information and has no executable forward value.

data.four_hour_bar_rule: UTC-anchored left-labelled 4-hour bars; exactly 16 consecutive valid 15-minute rows required; incomplete or gap-crossing bars rejected
data.lineage: Development history has been inspected by earlier BTC/ETH relationship and causal-model research. It can reject this mechanism but cannot provide independent promotion evidence.

primary_model.decision_grid: end of each complete UTC 4-hour bar
primary_model.rolling_regression: OLS with intercept of BTC 4-hour return on ETH 4-hour return using only the previous 180 complete contiguous 4-hour bars
primary_model.residual_threshold: 10th percentile of the previous 180 causal BTC residuals, excluding the current residual
context: current completed ETH 4-hour log return strictly positive
mean of completed BTC and ETH simple 24-hour returns strictly positive
primary_model.entry_condition: current BTC residual is at or below its causal rolling 10th percentile and every context condition passes
primary_model.entry: BTC at the first 15-minute open after the completed 4-hour bar
primary_model.exit: BTC at the 15-minute open exactly 24 hours after entry
primary_model.overlap_policy: ignore new signals while a BTC position is open
primary_model.sizing: 25 percent of current marked account equity, capped by available cash; no leverage

matched_controls.btc_buy_hold: 25 percent of initial equity held in BTC for the development interval
matched_controls.btc_self_reversal: BTC 4-hour return at or below its own causal rolling 10th percentile while BTC 24-hour return is positive; no ETH feature
matched_controls.joint_risk_on_every_24h: enter BTC at the first eligible joint-positive 24-hour context after the previous control exit; no residual or ETH-direction gate

calendar_matched_random.eligible_pool: non-signal complete 4-hour timestamps with positive joint 24-hour context and a valid 24-hour future BTC execution path
calendar_matched_random.matching: one timestamp from the same UTC calendar month for each primary signal
calendar_matched_random.statistic: mean primary-cost 24-hour BTC return on allocated capital

decision_rule: Any failed gate rejects this experiment ID before any forward or paper promotion. Sensitivities are robustness diagnostics, not alternate candidates to select after seeing results.
promotion_blockers: The development interval and related BTC/ETH feature family were previously inspected.
A passing development result would require a separately frozen genuinely prospective partition before paper-promotion review.
ETH is context only; this experiment does not authorize ETH orders or a BTC/ETH rotation.
research_basis: Published BTC/ETH lead-lag evidence is mixed and reports little reliably exploitable hourly/daily price discovery, so fixed-lag direction is not assumed.
Time-varying correlation and bidirectional volatility spillovers motivate a rolling conditional residual rather than a fixed correlation or lagging indicator crossover.
The null is expected to be competitive; a negative result closes this exact catch-up mechanism without threshold tuning.
